question: At an identical budget of genuine guard refits, does a worst-context masked vote improve the choice among equally compressed candidates beyond deletion fraction and a Gain tie-break?
scope: Retrospective on all 41 feasible archived PMLB guard folds, plus one locally prospectively specified UCI Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits study (ID 80) using the official train and test files, separately reported. No further datasets or thresholds chosen on these results.
learner: Shared 100-tree single-thread CPU XGBoost, donor Compact Gain order and anchor verified on fitting and proposal rows. PMLB fold seeds 20421+fold. Optdigits uses seed 20421, stratified split 75% fit and 25% remaining official train rows, split remaining in equal proposal/guard halves as in PMLB. Official test rows withheld; test measures are per example; writer identifiers unavailable in the feature files.
pool: At each distinct strictly smaller width ceil(A/4), ceil(A/2), ceil(3A/4), offer the Gain prefix and up to seven other distinct subsets drawn uniformly without replacement from anchor columns at that width. If at most eight supports exist, include all. numpy seed [81027, task index, fold, width] for draws and [72291, task index, fold, width] for the uniform tie order. Task index in the original fixed list, or 100 for Optdigits. Small anchors permit fewer widths or no deletion. These folds stay in the denominator.
primary: One candidate guard refit at ceil(A/2), i.e. a half-anchor width ceiling and one chance to retain that compression. Half-width equal to the anchor means no deletion and no candidate refit.
secondary: One candidate guard refit at each of the up to three distinct strict widths. Evaluate every shortlisted width and choose the smallest guard-passing width, else the anchor.
methods: Common widths and candidate identities. fraction_gain breaks within-width ties by smallest sum of ranks in the training Gain order, then column IDs (thus includes the prefix). vote_gain maximizes minimum approvals over the full separating family with four original panels on proposal rows, tie broken identically. fraction_lottery and vote_lottery use the same uniformly preassigned tie order rather than Gain, to measure the effect without a useful within-width tie-break. Do not use guard or test labels to form shortlists.
evaluation: For each policy compute metrics for A/S trained on fit+proposal, assessed only on disjoint guard rows. Accept subject to inherited joint 3% relative AUC/accuracy and 5% rare positive AP tolerance. Freeze supports before final fitting on all development and scoring on outer rows. The primary value is safe fraction of anchor columns saved, u=(1-k/A)*I(no outer tolerance breach). A fallback scores zero. Also report errors, AUC, accuracy, selected fraction, actual guard fit counts and candidates that differ. A prospective deployment should charge time and any additional cost of a breach. No guard is an oracle.
compute: Time shared preparation, ranking and pool creation, per-width marginal mask scoring, per-candidate guard fits, imputation and final fits separately. Charge every arm for its components, reusing shared identical fits in the benchmark. Each budget's vote starts cold. Equivalent shortcuts may stop a candidate when its min reaches zero. Not balanced cold-process timings; report measured component sums and cost not speed claims.
uncertainty: Primary paired value difference vote_gain vs fraction_gain: average fold differences within task then tasks equally, paired task cluster percentile bootstrap 30000 draws seed 33119, all three or two folds kept together. Report all positive, tied and adverse tasks/folds, same comparison for alternative budgets and tie-breaks as descriptive. Never pool UCI with these tasks.
